articles.headline: Notes by the Way, No. III (travel letter)
articles.author: J. M. Brown
articles.summary: In the Communications department: 'The morning of the 21st of August I left with Mrs. B. to attend an Emancipation Celebration at Frederick, Md.' A travel letter describing a large Emancipation Day procession at Frederick City and a mass meeting at Bethel Church, Baltimore, to hear John Mercer Langston, whose address (reprinted from the Baltimore American) is appended. Signed J. M. Brown, Baltimore, Aug. 27th, 1867.

articles.headline: The Book Depository of the A.M.E. Church (advertisement, changed address)
articles.summary: Standing ad: 'THE BOOK DEPOSITORY of the AFRICAN M.E. CHURCH, No. 631 Pine Street, PHILADELPHIA.' Keeps on hand Discipline, Sunday-School books and sermon books, Question Books, Hymn Books Nos. 1, 2 and 3, blank books, stationery, inks, pens, and Developer black books. NOTE: the printed number is 631 Pine (confirmed from both the 09-14 and the clearer 09-21 printing), an address update from the 619 Pine of earlier printings (matching the office move to 631 Pine).

articles.headline: Rev. I. R. Gates' Macamoose (advertisement, changed depot address)
articles.summary: 'Rev. I. R. Gates' MACAMOOSE. The Great Indian Remedy for the Blood. A Most Complete Health Restorer.' Price $1.50 per bottle. 'For sale by Druggists generally, and at Macamoose Depot, No. 513 Race street, Philadelphia, Pa.' NOTE: depot address 513 Race Street differs from the 1230 Wood St. / 1618 N. 11th St. recorded in Run #97 -- an apparent new/changed depot location.

articles.headline: A Rare Chance for a First-Class Dentist (notice -- late Dr. Jas. McC. Crummill's practice)
articles.summary: 'A RARE CHANCE for a First-Class Dentist! Wanted -- a first-class Surgical and Mechanical Dentist, desiring to secure the advantages of a long-established business, to take the Office and Laboratory of the late Dr. Jas. Mc. C. Crummill. The Doctor having, for over twenty years, occupied the premises and carried on the business... The establishment is fully supplied with instruments and implements... For terms and further information, apply to Sarah Mc. C. Crummill, 449 North Third Street, Philadelphia.' Dated May. Runs weekly in all three September issues. FLAG: dated late May (one month term), so it may already be in the database from the May/June printings (Run #100); included because it names a Black Philadelphia dentist and his widow. Street number best read 449 (so read on 09-21 and 09-28; 09-14 looked like 419).
people: surgical and mechanical dentist, deceased (late Dr.)
